items.cite: Joseph N. Straus, *Remaking the Past: Musical Modernism and the Influence of the Tonal Tradition* (Harvard University Press, 1990).
items.note: Examines musical modernism in relation to inherited tonal traditions; a theoretical counterpart to the specific borrowing practices studied by Burkholder.

items.cite: Kevin Korsyn, ‘Towards a New Poetics of Musical Influence’, *Music Analysis* 10, nos. 1–2 (1991).
items.note: A theoretical treatment of musical influence. Use its interpretative arguments alongside documentary evidence, not as a substitute for it.

items.cite: J. Peter Burkholder, ‘Borrowing’, *Grove Music Online* (Oxford University Press, 2001).
items.note: A reference article specifically on musical borrowing; the link supplies the publisher-deposited bibliographic record.

items.cite: J. Peter Burkholder, *All Made of Tunes: Charles Ives and the Uses of Musical Borrowing* (Yale University Press, 2004 paperback).
items.note: Treats borrowing as a compositional practice, not merely a list of recognisable quotations.

items.cite: Charles Rosen, *The Classical Style: Haydn, Mozart, Beethoven*, expanded edition (W. W. Norton, 1998 paperback).
items.note: Explains musical conventions through Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven; the expanded edition includes a chapter on late Beethoven.
